entries.title: Job 2:1
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content:
1 Satan appearing again before God, obtains further leave to tempt Job. 7 He smites him with sore boils. 9 Job reproves his wife, who moved him to curse God. 11 His three friends console with him in silence.

Again. 1:6; Isa 6:1,2; Lu 1:19; Heb 1:14

entries.title: Job 2:3
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content: Hast thou. 1:1,8; 9:20; Ge 6:9; Ps 37:37; Php 3:12; 1Pe 5:10 an upright. Pr 11:8; 13:6; 14:2; 15:8; 16:17 holdeth. 1:21,22; 13:15; 27:5,6; Ps 26:1; 41:12; Jas 1:12; 1Pe 1:7 thou movedst. 1:11 destroy him. Heb. swallow him up. 2Sa 20:20 without. 9:17; Joh 9:3

entries.title: Job 2:6
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content: Behold. 1:12 but. or, only. save. 38:10,11; Ps 65:7; Lu 8:29-33; 22:31,32; 1Co 10:13; Re 2:10 Re 20:1,2,7 his life.By {naphsho,} "his soul," Maimonides understands "his mind," or intellectual powers.

entries.title: Job 2:7
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content:
So went. 1Ki 22:22 sore boils.{Shechin r�,} supposed to be the {Judham,} or black leprosy, of the Arabs, termed Elephantiasis by the Greeks, from its rendering the skin, like that of the elephant, scabrous, dark coloured, and furrowed all over with tubercles. This loathsome and most afflictive disease is accompanied with most intolerable itching.

30:17-19,30; Ex 9:9-11; De 28:27,35; Re 16:11 from the sole. Isa 1:6; 3:17
